A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOMOK framework and overlapping experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original link-prediction results on four MMKG benchmarks, alongside robustness experiments, ablations, efficiency measurements and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds FB15K-237 results, additional benchmark metrics and further ablations in Appendix C.3.

M1.justification: ReMoKE, MuJoD, ExID, their objectives and the training/inference procedures remain unchanged. Equation 3 adds relation subscripts to embeddings already described as relation-guided in v2; this clarifies notation without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Appendix C.3.2 adds FB15K-237 link prediction to the four existing MMKG benchmarks. The task remains MMKG completion, and the original noisy-modality, missing-modality and sparse-link scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The original main comparison retains the same 20 baselines. The new FB15K-237 comparison in v3 Table 7 separately reports MoSE-AI, MoSE-BI and MoSE-MI, extending the explicitly compared ensemble variants beyond v2's single MoSE row.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 expands the stated embedding-dimension search from {200, 250, 300} to {200, 250, 300, 400, 500}. Existing splits, metrics and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. This establishes a revised reported tuning protocol, without establishing that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Table 8 extends the complete modality-contribution and component-removal ablations to MKG-Y and KVC16K. Consequently, all four original benchmarks now have these checks, substantially broadening evidence about the components' contributions across datasets. The existing robustness tests and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or random seeds, or reports confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The main-table scores and original ablation scores are unchanged. v3 Tables 6–8 add Hit@3/Hit@10 results for MKG-W/MKG-Y, FB15K-237 results including MOMOK MRR 36.08, and additional ablation outcomes. Figure 4 also reverses the loss-weight labels while retaining the plotted values, moving the displayed peak from 0.0001 to 0.001 and conflicting with unchanged Section 5.5.

T1.justification: The CLUB theorems, KL-divergence condition and proofs move from Appendix A to Appendix B without substantive mathematical changes. Replacing x and y with embedding variables Vi and Vj connects the existing derivation to the model but does not introduce new assumptions or results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about relation-guided experts, mutual-information disentanglement, performance, robustness and interpretability. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 expands discussion of fine versus coarse ranking performance, acknowledges MoSE-BI's stronger FB15K-237 Hit scores alongside different embedding sizes, and explains dataset-dependent ablation effects through the strong TuckER foundation. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 removes v2 Table 6 and Appendix B.3, losing the exact per-dataset learning rates, selected embedding dimensions and 2000-epoch training budget. These replication settings are not relocated elsewhere. General implementation details and the code/data URL remain, while Appendix C.3.2 newly discloses embedding sizes for the FB15K-237 comparison.

R1.justification: New Appendix A organizes existing MMKGC approaches into fusion, ensemble and negative-sampling methods, explicitly positioning MOMOK between fusion and ensemble approaches. v3 also adds several Liang and Zhao citations and removes Chen et al. (2022), while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. Changes include conference headers, expanded affiliations, acknowledgments, limited wording corrections, aligned mathematical notation and appendix reorganization around new related-work and supplementary-results sections.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the appendix's results presentation with separate tables for complete benchmark metrics, FB15K-237 comparisons and additional ablations. It moves dataset statistics from the main text, removes the hyperparameter table, shortens Figure 2's caption, and relocates and reformats Figure 4, including reversed loss-weight labels.

improvement.justification: Tables 6–8 improve empirical completeness through additional metrics, another benchmark and broader component checks. However, removing the exact training configurations weakens reproducibility, and Figure 4 introduces a contradiction about the best loss weight. These concrete gains and losses leave the overall direction uncertain; the PDFs neither resolve the plotting inconsistency nor replace the removed replication information.
